status: drafted via multi-agent workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text, adversarially fact-checked and corrected
notes: Grounded directly in E:/Unity/Clicker_Genesis/Assets/Resources/Verses/Geneva/2_kings_12.json (all 25 chapters, 719 verses read in full) and cross-checked against the already-validated KJV 2Kings.json for tier-naming inspiration only, not copied structurally. CONTENT VERDICT: this Geneva text tells the exact same 25-chapter regnal narrative as KJV 2 Kings, in the same order, with no missing or added episodes — unlike the Ethiopian "Ezra" case, there is no structural/content divergence here, only orthographic and lexical ones. REAL LEXICAL DIFFERENCES FOUND (verified by reading, not assumed): (1) Geneva systematically renders "Syria"/"Syrians" as "Aram"/"Aramites" throughout every chapter (3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 13, 16) — a genuine, consistent translation choice, not a one-off spelling. (2) "Assyria" is rendered "Asshur" throughout. (3) Elijah is spelled "Eliiah" (i/j interchangeable in 1560 English). (4) Jehu appears as "Iehu"; Jordan as "Iorden"; Jezebel as "Iezebel"; Jezreel as "Izreel"; chariot as "charet." (5) Benhadad is hyphenated "Ben-hadad" (vs. KJV's one-word "Benhadad"). (6) "Tiglath Pileser" is printed as two words (vs. KJV's one-word "Tiglathpileser"). (7) Sennacherib is spelled "Saneherib." (8) 2 Kings 20:12's Babylonian envoy's king is "Berodach Baladan" — TWO words in this Geneva text, a real difference from the KJV 2Kings.json's own documented note that KJV uses the one-word "Berodachbaladan" here. (9) "Nebuchadnezzar" is consistently hyphenated "Nebuchad-nezzar." (10) 25:27's "Evilmerodach" is hyphenated "Euil-merodach." (11) 23:29's "Pharaohnechoh" is printed as two words, "Pharaoh Nechoh." (12) Azariah/Uzziah of Judah is called "Vzziah" at 15:13, 15:30, 15:32 and "Azariah" everywhere else in his own regnal notices (1, 6, 7, 17, 23, 27) — the same internal double-naming already flagged in the KJV file, confirmed present in Geneva too. NAMING COLLISIONS RE-VERIFIED AGAINST THIS SPECIFIC TEXT (all confirmed actually present in the Geneva wording, not assumed from KJV): two men named Ahaziah (king of Israel, ch.1; king of Judah, ch.8-9); "Iehoram"/"Ioram" used for both the king of Israel (ch.3) and his brother-in-law the king of Judah (ch.8), who are explicitly siblings-in-law via Athaliah; "Iehoash"/"Ioash" used interchangeably within the SAME king's own passages for both Judah's boy-king (11:21 "Iehoash" / 12:19 "Ioash") and, separately, Israel's later king (13:9 "Ioash" / 13:10 "Iehoash") — two different men, both called by both spellings; two men named Jehoahaz (Israel, 13:1, son of Jehu; Judah, 23:31, son of Josiah); "Zachariah" used for both Jeroboam II's son (15:8) and Hezekiah's maternal grandfather (18:2); Shallum the usurper-king (15:10) vs. Shallum husband of Huldah (22:14); "Ieremiah of Libnah" (23:31, 24:18, father of two queens) explicitly not the prophet Jeremiah. No role:"law" tier is used — like KJV, this book is regnal narrative genre throughout; the theological indictment of Israel's fall (17:7-23) and the rediscovered book of the law (22-23) are folded into the relevant kings' own manager entries as things they personally enact, not treated as a standalone law/theme tier. All character ids are suffixed "_geneva" to avoid collision with the existing KJV CharacterIndex.
